evidence.reason: In boot() the child is spawned with Popen at 712-713, but the recorder write at 714-715 sits outside the try at 716 whose except/finally (730-755) is the only path that stops the scope, terminates/waits the child and closes the log FD. If Recorder.append raises (unwritable/detached journal, disk full), that error propagates before the protection starts: the spawned systemd-run/QEMU child and the opened qemu.log descriptor are left behind while the caller releases the run lock, and a pending child can execute after the CLI exits. The function clearly intends to clean up on any post-spawn failure (the except block covers pid-file, identity-write and process failures), so this escape is an ordinary cleanup defect in existing intended behavior, not a new requirement. Moving the append inside the protected try (keeping it on the successful path before the wait loop) is the smallest fix and needs no owner judgment.
